I will keep to the crop pattern I know best in Quzhou: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I am 73, so I will not chase complicated crops that need more labor, more market watching, or more risk. Grain is what I know, the machines fit it, and the weather and soils here fit it too. At the start of the season, the winter wheat is already in the ground from last autumn, so I will manage that through harvest, then I will seed summer maize right after. I am assuming I am working 10 mu of land, because no land area was given.

For the wheat, I will stay with an improved variety, use moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few key times, and keep pesticide sprays limited to what is needed for disease and insects. I will use rotary tillage before the next wheat cycle because it is easier on my body than deep ploughing and still works well enough for me. After wheat harvest, I will put the same 10 mu straight into hybrid summer maize. I will do that because maize after wheat is the steadiest rotation here, and no-tillage or reduced tillage saves me labor and time in the hot harvest window. I will keep fertilizer and water at practical levels, not extreme ones, because I care more about stable output and manageable work than pushing for the highest possible yield.
